image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a white coral fungus (likely Ramaria or Clavulina species) growing on a forest floor covered in brown decaying leaves and patches of green moss. The fungus features a complex, multi-branched structure rising from a central base, with numerous cylindrical branches dividing into finer, club-shaped tips. The color is predominantly creamy white to pale beige.
